statement_record.book: A subcategory D of C is a subcollection of the objects and a subcollection of the morphisms of C closed under: containing the domain and codomain of each of its morphisms, containing the identity of each of its objects, and containing the composite of any composable pair of its morphisms.
statement_record.intree: Record Subcategory := { sobj : C → Type; shom {x y : C} : sobj x → sobj y → (x ~> y) → Type; scomp ... : shom oy oz f → shom ox oy g → shom ox oz (f ∘ g); sid {x : C} (ox : sobj x) : shom ox ox (@id C x) }.

evidence.intree_statement: Definition Quotient (C : Category) (R : HomRel C) `{@HomCongruence C R} : Category := {| obj := @obj C; hom := @hom C; homset := fun x y => {| equiv := R x y; setoid_equiv := Quotient_equivalence x y |}; id := @id C; compose := @compose C; compose_respects := fun x y z f f' Hf g g' Hg => cong_comp Hf Hg; ... |}.

Class HomCongruence {C : Category} (R : HomRel C) : Type := { cong_incl {x y} {f g : x ~> y} : f ≈ g → R x y f g; cong_sym ... ; cong_trans ... ; cong_comp {x y z} {f f' : y ~> z} {g g' : x ~> y} : R y z f f' → R x y g g' → R x z (f ∘ g) (f' ∘ g') }.

Definition QuotientProj : C ⟶ Quotient C R := Build_Functor C (Quotient C R) (fun x => x) (fun x y f => f) (fun x y f g Hfg => cong_incl Hfg) (fun x => cong_refl (@id C x)) (fun x y z f g => cong_refl (f ∘ g)).

statement_record.book: Exercise 1.1.iv: a congruence is an equivalence relation ~ on the hom-sets of a category respected by pre- and postcomposition (f ~ g implies hfk ~ hgk). (i) Show that for a congruence ~ on C there is a quotient category with the same objects as C and with morphisms the ~-classes of parallel C-morphisms. (ii) Prove that homotopy is a congruence on Top — if f, g : X → Y are homotopic and k : W → X, h : Y → Z are continuous, then hfk and hgk are homotopic — exhibiting Htpy as a quotient of Top.
statement_record.intree: Class HomCongruence {C : Category} (R : HomRel C) : Type := { cong_incl : f ≈ g → R x y f g; cong_sym; cong_trans; cong_comp : R y z f f' → R x y g g' → R x z (f ∘ g) (f' ∘ g') }.  Definition Quotient (C : Category) (R : HomRel C) `{@HomCongruence C R} : Category := {| obj := @obj C; hom := @hom C; homset := fun x y => {| equiv := R x y; ... |}; ... |}.
statement_record.strength_comparison: Part (i): same, in the setoid idiom. The quotient does not literally form equivalence CLASSES — it keeps C's objects and morphisms and coarsens the hom-setoid's ≈ to R, which in a setoid library is the faithful rendering of 'morphisms are the ~-classes' (Construction/Quotient.v:250-253 documents exactly this). `cong_comp` is two-sided compatibility in one field and is equivalent to Riehl's `f ~ g ⇒ hfk ~ hgk` given reflexivity, which `cong_incl` supplies; `Quotient_equivalence` (:241) derives the equivalence-relation clause. intree-stronger on this clause: `QuotientProj` and a universal property are provided, which the exercise does not ask for. Part (ii): absent — the library has no Top and no homotopy relation, so 'homotopy is a congruence' and 'Htpy is a quotient of Top' have no carrier.

gap: Clause (ii) is entirely missing: there is no category of topological spaces and no homotopy relation in-tree, so neither 'homotopy is a congruence on Top' nor 'Htpy = Top/homotopy' can be stated. Note also a presentational point that would matter to any consumer: `HomRel` is Prop-valued (`Definition HomRel (C : Category) := ∀ x y : C, (x ~> y) → (x ~> y) → Prop`), so a congruence carrying data (e.g. a chosen homotopy) does not fit the class as stated.

evidence.intree_statement: Definition Opposite `(C : Category) : Category := {| obj := @obj C; hom := fun x y => @hom C y x; homset := fun x y => @homset C y x; id := @id C; compose := fun _ _ _ f g => g ∘ f; compose_respects := fun x y z f g fg h i hi => @compose_respects C z y x h i hi f g fg; id_left := fun x y f => @id_right C y x f; id_right := fun x y f => @id_left C y x f; comp_assoc := fun x y z w f g h => @comp_assoc_sym C w z y x h g f; comp_assoc_sym := fun x y z w f g h => @comp_assoc C w z y x h g f |}.

statement_record.book: Definition 1.2.1: C^op has the same objects as C and one morphism f^op : Y → X for each f : X → Y of C, with identities id_X^op and composition f^op · g^op := (g · f)^op, defined exactly when g · f is; associativity and unitality hold precisely because they hold in C, so C^op carries the same information as C — the syntactic self-duality of the axioms.
statement_record.intree: Definition Opposite `(C : Category) : Category := {| obj := @obj C; hom := fun x y => @hom C y x; id := @id C; compose := fun _ _ _ f g => g ∘ f; id_left := fun x y f => @id_right C y x f; id_right := fun x y f => @id_left C y x f; comp_assoc := fun x y z w f g h => @comp_assoc_sym C w z y x h g f; ... |}.  Lemma op_invol {C : Category} : (C^op)^op = C.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger. Every clause of the definition is present and each law is discharged by literally handing back C's own law with the arguments permuted — which is precisely Riehl's 'the axioms hold because they hold in C' made into the proof term (id_left := id_right, comp_assoc := comp_assoc_sym). Riehl's f ↦ f^op renaming is definitional here (hom[C^op] x y is convertible with hom[C] y x, with `op`/`unop` the identity on the underlying arrow); the library goes past the book by proving the involution STRICTLY, `op_invol : (C^op)^op = C` on the nose (=), where Riehl only claims C^op 'carries exactly the same information'. The header at :80-96 discusses this design fork against agda-unimath/1Lab/agda-categories.

Every near-miss the record lists is real and correctly characterized as a near-miss: Theory/Functor.v:227 `fobj_iso : Proper (Isomorphism ==> Isomorphism) fobj[F]` (preservation, not the criterion), Theory/Functor.v:355 `FullyFaithful : ∀ x y, F x ≅ F y → x ≅ y` and Theory/Equivalence/Limit.v:335 `ff_reflects_isos : ReflectsIsos F` (OBJECT-level conservativity), Functor/Hom.v:85/96/109 (`Yoneda_Faithful`, `Yoneda_Full`, `Yoneda_Embedding'` — the hom-set bijection induced by `Curried_Hom` on MORPHISMS OF C^op, a different bijection from Riehl's f_*), Functor/Hom/Yoneda.v:231/253.
